One of the primary issues with domain adaptive pedestrian detection is the phenomenon of false positives.  We introduce an innovative, unsupervised box re-ranking method that effectively addresses this challenge.  We break down the detection task into two components: ranking the box scores based on confidence and fine-tuning the box scores to minimize false positives.  We combine the two stages in an end-to-end framework, the Fast Pedestrian Adapter, which leverages cross-attention mechanisms to enhance the box score.  Experimental findings on the Cityscape dataset demonstrate the significant efficacy of our method in reducing false positives.

This study presents an innovative method for enhancing low-quality music recordings made on consumer devices, which often include distortions like noise, echoes, and distortions. Combining two techniques, our approach utilizes spectral mapping to revert the spectral content of the input audio to a normal frequency spectrum and applies time-stretching to prolong the duration of the signal. The power of deep learning is leveraged by training a deep autoencoder on a synthesized audio dataset and demonstrating that our method can significantly improve vocal signals in poor quality audio. The results of our method were tested on a publicly accessible dataset, demonstrating substantial enhancements to low-quality music recordings.

Our primary objective is to examine the impact of a virtual object's point of release on the User Interface (UI) in throwing motions. Our findings indicate that a UI element can be effectively manipulated by multiple release points, provided the difference between them is minimal. In our study, participants performed a throwing motion to interact with a UI element, which had its point of release either randomly changed or kept consistent, from a fixed height. Upon analysis, it was discovered that: (1) UI elements influenced by multiple release points can be effectively thrown, and (2) when multiple release points are used, the UI trajectory tends to complete a circular motion, while a single point results in a more linear path. (3) When multiple release points are employed, users can interact with larger and lighter UI elements compared to those with a single point of release. (4) Multiple release points allow users to interact with heavier UI elements, eliminating the need to aim for a specific release location.

To incorporate syntax-aware decoding into Neural Machine Translation (NMT), a new tree structured MT model called top-down MT was developed. The model, based on a recent tree structured VT-MT model, generates output sequences in an orderly fashion. It was enhanced with syntactic connections to generate more coherent and syntax-aware output sequences. Experiments in multiple language pairs, including both resource-rich and rare languages, demonstrated the model's effectiveness. The results showed that top-down MT significantly outperforms other MT models, with an improvement of 1.0-1.4 points BLEU score.

The availability of extensive surface reaction data in astrochemistry is significantly limited, with only a limited number of accurate surface binding energies available for review. Various databases and publications have attempted to compile surface reaction data, including the Surface Binding Energy Database by the ExoChemistry Reaction Database, the Reaction Binding Energy Database, and the Astrochemical Surface Binding Energy Database. However, the reaction binding energies listed in the SBE database lack clarity, and some conflicting entries are present. A comprehensive search through the literature revealed 110 surface binding energy evaluations, corresponding to 170 reactions, which were further analyzed. Of these, 11 reactions, spanning CO, H2O, NH3, and H2, were identified as universally agreed upon with binding energies below 1 kJ/mol, while 106 literature values exceeded 1 kJ/mol. A compilation of the literature, including the Surface Binding Energy Database, revealed 11 universally accepted reactions and demonstrated that the SBE database contains 12 incorrectly listed entries. A new platform, the Binding Energy Evaluation Platform, has been created to provide a distribution of quantum chemical surface binding energy, which can be used to identify and eliminate unreliable literature values. When applied to the SBE database, the Binding Energy Evaluation Platform successfully identified incorrect entries.

A multiplicative stochastic process with lognormally distributed lower bounds is studied, where a new statistical model is developed based on a stochastic process whose lower bounds depend on sample data. The model's parameters, including the mean and standard deviation of the normal distribution underlying the process, are estimated using two methods - maximum likelihood estimation and moment estimation. Mathematical expressions for the bias and standard error of the estimated parameters are derived. Additionally, an analysis of sample maximum distribution is provided to determine bias and standard error of the sample maximum. The model's applicability in predicting the durability of reinforced concrete structures in marine environments is also demonstrated through simulation-based evaluation.

We offer novel approaches to evaluate the expectation values of random Clifford networks, also known as random Clifford, using two distinct methods, one of which is suitable for implementation on quantum devices with limited capabilities, utilizing low-depth circuits, and the other tailored for powerful quantum machines, utilizing high-depth circuits. The first method relies on calculating shadows using single-qubit measurements, interconnecting them with Clifford networks, and utilizing a computational technique, referred to as efficient matching method, to determine the shadows. The second method employs deep networks, interconnecting Clifford gates, and directly calculating the shadow values, also referred to as direct sampling method. The first method is demonstrated to yield similar results to existing efficient algorithms, while the second method outperforms them in terms of sample complexity, and can be used to estimate the average value of random Clifford networks more efficiently. Our approach may be applied to analyze quantum circuits composed of Clifford gates, including those used in quantum algorithms, such as Shor's algorithm, and other protocols, such as quantum error correction.

The researchers in this study have derived the asymptotic behavior of the reflection coefficient $|s_{j,k}|$ for the Darboux transform, derived from solving the Schrodinger equation with reflectionless potential $V_{j,k}(x,t)$, obtained from the complex plane's standard fundamental domain. They found that for the generic case, $|s_{j,k}|$ is upper-bounded by the spatial parameter $t_j$, and for specific scenarios where the fundamental domain reduces to two or one pole configurations, specific upper-bounds on the reflection coefficient were also determined.

Deep language models have demonstrated exceptional text classification capabilities, but this comes with significant computational and data privacy drawbacks. The current study explores the application of transformation-based data augmentation techniques, known as Sibylviant transformations, to enhance robustness and defend against model inversion attacks. By manipulating input data, Sibylviant transformations prevent the model from learning sensitive features, including sensitive attributes and adversarial examples, and instead encourage a focus on more representative data characteristics. Our research examines four types of transformations, evaluates their effectiveness in the context of benchmark datasets, and investigates the impact of feature selection on mitigating model sensitivity.

Researchers aim to create meta-learning algorithms that can quickly adapt to unfamiliar tasks by learning to represent new data in an unseen domain. In this paper, we propose and prove the effectiveness of novel meta-learning algorithms that are guaranteed to produce optimal linear transformations for representation. Our current approach, Meta-IRL, uses an iterative process to find the best linear transformation, while Meta-SVM offers a computationally efficient alternative. Both algorithms are designed to work with a diverse set of distribution shifts. Our results show that, under ideal conditions, it is possible to find the best linear transformation, but this task generally requires an infinite number of iterations. However, by using strong regularisation, we are able to prove that Meta-SVM converges to a unique solution. Our experiments demonstrate that, in practice, both algorithms perform similarly and often outperform state-of-the-art methods, especially on challenging real-world datasets.

High-performing multilingual models from the Transformer family have seen significant success, yet they have large parameter counts, making them impractical for deployment on resource-constrained devices. To address this issue, we explore two primary strategies for creating lightweight language models: structured quantization and distillation. While effective, both methods have their limitations. Quantization, for instance, often results in a considerable drop in performance, whereas distillation has its own set of challenges. To overcome these issues, we introduce a new structured quantization method called partial quantization, which combines knowledge distillation and structured quantization. We demonstrate its effectiveness and stability in model compression by comparing it to existing methods through numerical and statistical analyses.

We introduce a hypergraph with a well-defined density parameter $\alpha$ between 0 and 1, from which we derive the natural Lagrangian density for this density parameter. By selecting $\alpha$ as the ratio $k-1$ over $k+1$ for the $(k+1)$-graph, we obtain the Lagrangian density as the square root of 2 minus 2 times the square of $\alpha$. In this case, our approach provides evidence that a density parameter of the form $p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are positive integers, will yield a rational Lagrangian density if and only if a previously identified condition is met.

The accuracy of deep learning models heavily relies on extensive labelled datasets. For chest X-ray segmentation tasks, obtaining sufficient labelled data can be costly and time-consuming. To mitigate this issue, we investigated how image manipulation techniques such as rotations, flips, and color modifications affect segmentation performance. By employing these image enhancement strategies, we found that models trained on a smaller labelled dataset achieved comparable results to those trained on the largest available labelled dataset. Specifically, we achieved an improvement of 4.1% and 8.2% in mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) scores on two datasets using rotated and color-modified x-ray augmentations, respectively. Furthermore, a combination of these image enhancement strategies demonstrated the most significant boost in mean mIoU score of 8.2% on the AMOS dataset compared to the unmodified model.

The task of image captioning has been traditionally addressed using a two-stage process. The first stage involves a CNN-ViT-based image encoder, while the second stage employs a BERT-based language model to generate a caption. While this approach has been effective, it has a significant limitation in that it lacks the ability to generate diverse images with varying levels of detail. To overcome this issue, we introduce a novel training method called prompt learning, which enables us to generate images with different levels of details. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated on two public datasets, where it results in a 1.1 point improvement on COCO Captioning evaluation metrics and 0.7 point improvement on ScanCap evaluation metrics. Additionally, it has been shown that this method can be easily integrated into existing image captioning models with minimal additional parameters.

As autonomous systems become increasingly prevalent, there is a pressing need to address the potential for harm in the context of AI. This discussion focuses on harm caused to individuals rather than society. A fundamental issue in determining harm is its reliance on causality, a concept that is often elusive in its own right. This study sets out to address both questions by developing a mathematical representation of harm within the framework of causal models, specifically for cases where an agent has control. It is demonstrated that such harm can unambiguously be identified in certain scenarios, with a notable implication being that in decision-making scenarios, one's intention plays a pivotal role in defining harm.

This study showcases MMLSpark, an innovative open-source library that integrates the power of PyTorch and Spark AI for efficient distributed deep learning on Apache Spark. By leveraging this integration, data can be captured from distributed datasets and processed in a unified manner. The custom-built data capture feature and the integration with Spark AI enable the efficient handling of text and image data directly within Spark data. The extensive integration with MLLib and MLflow allows for model analysis and deployment within existing ecosystems. The three core deep learning builders in MMLSpark support various use cases, including classification and regression, and demonstrate scalability as evidenced by experiments with synthetic datasets.

Speech to text translation has long been the focus of research, with the ultimate goal of achieving zero-shot translation from speech to text without any parallel data available. This challenge is complicated by the fact that speech to text translation typically requires parallel training data, and there are few systems capable of handling this constraint. In response, we have developed a new framework for zero-shot speech to text translation, utilizing pre-trained language models to accurately transcribe speech from speech to text without the necessity for parallel data. Our approach involves using autoencoders and supervised fine-tuning to accurately transcribe speech from speech to text, and we have demonstrated that this method outperforms the current state-of-the-art on the SpSpeechTranslation corpus, with significant improvements across a range of language pairs, with speech to text translation from speech to text achieving a word error rate of 35.5, compared to the previous best of 37.9, and speech to text translation from speech to text achieving a word error rate of 43.5, compared to the previous best of 45.7.

This work introduces a novel extension of the traditional heat conduction theory, encompassing cases where heat is generated by chemical processes, as detailed in [1]. We examine the evolution equations describing such systems under dynamic boundary conditions, encompassing both finite element approximations and numerical experiments that validate the theoretical analysis.

The increasing adoption of renewable energy technologies in home environments, such as photovoltaic systems, has significant implications for the operation of low-voltage networks. Due to the intermittent and unpredictable nature of solar energy, forecasting the daily energy consumption at the level of single buildings or groups of similar structures is crucial. In this context, this paper presents an innovative approach to forecasting the daily consumption of low-voltage networks, combining individual predictions to generate accurate energy profiles. Notably, the large variability of consumption in LV networks poses significant challenges, which this study aims to address through the development of a novel forecast fusion method, as well as an investigation into the prediction of daily peaks. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated by comparing it with the current state-of-the-art on publicly available data.

The growth of machine learning algorithms has not entirely resolved the issues affecting AI performance, mainly due to the lack of relevant data. Kernels and transfer learning have shown some progress in addressing knowledge integration. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the current state and the need for developing better knowledge integration techniques to effectively tackle key AI challenges. Kernels and transfer learning have shown some progress in addressing knowledge integration within knowledge learning paradigms. This paper provides the most up-to-date "roadmap" of knowledge integration within the machine learning field.

In the fight against COVID-19, computer-aided diagnosis plays a vital role by providing essential support to medical professionals in identifying and segmenting pulmonary embolisms on CT scans. The current deep learning-based methods for this purpose rely on image classification and localization, which can be flawed due to the presence of imaging biases. These biases can be minimized by training deep learning models on a larger dataset of CT scans, but existing research has primarily focused on strict supervision, which is not feasible due to the shortage of annotated data. In response, a weakly supervised approach is proposed, which can be effectively trained using only image-level labels and employs two types of supervision: a primary level of classification-based supervision and a secondary level of localization and segmentation. The proposed method has shown substantial improvements in various tasks, including detection, localization, and segmentation, by breaking down the challenges into simpler steps. The innovative framework can be utilized in a wide range of medical image analysis tasks, thus having the potential to significantly enhance the effectiveness of COVID-19 treatment.

This paper presents a detailed description of the methods used in the
deep learning-based method for automatic vertebra identification in
abdominal/pelvic computed tomography scans. The approach is based on the
assumption that spine curvature is a common occurrence, and proposes a
two-stage process. The first stage involves analyzing an axial slice to
determine the vertebrae involved and positioning the spine. The second
stage involves identifying vertebrae in a 3D volume. The underlying
methodology leverages the strengths of 2D and 3D deep learning to
optimize performance. The approach relies on a U-Net-based network
designed to produce vertebra segmentation masks, followed by an
optimization-based algorithm to generate accurate vertebrae centerlines
from these masks. The approach demonstrates competitive and robust
performance on the challenge dataset. The corresponding code is publicly
available on GitHub.

We're investigating the scattering of an electron in an ultrastrong coupling regime where it interacts with two modes of light within a cavity. This setup is analogous to a double Kronecker potential with an electron experiencing high interactions with the auxiliary light modes. As a result, electrons are initially captured by the light-matter system, getting trapped in quasi-stationary states, before they're emitted and detected by a third, detuned mode. The detected signal exhibits a distinct Fermi resonance pattern characterized by its vivid structure, providing a clear signature of the electron's capture by the ultrastrong coupling system. Moreover, analysis shows that the electron's interaction with the light modes generates a dynamical stabilization effect. Specifically, when the system is strongly coupled, vacuum fluctuations provide a form of "quantum friction" that counteracts the electron's decay. This phenomenon effectively protects the electron from being emitted, thus achieving a form of stabilization through the interaction with the ultrastrong coupling system.

In this research, we're enhancing our breakthrough quadruped design, named Atlas, which utilizes actuated elastic tendons to achieve exceptional torque density and impressive running capabilities. By integrating advanced control methods with this innovative design, we've developed a model-based predictive controller that successfully plans and executes complex locomotion trajectories in real-time, even in the face of significant dynamic distortions. Furthermore, our system incorporates a model-based reinforcement learning approach, where a neural network learns the dynamics of Atlas to provide efficient planning capabilities. Our study demonstrates the synergistic effect of expert-designed elastic designs and learned control strategies in achieving a remarkable range of locomotion behaviors on challenging outdoor surfaces.

We propose a novel variational method for calculating upper bounds of entanglement measures in a wide range of applications. The method yields impressive results when applied to randomly generated quantum states in multipartite systems, with the obtained bounds consistently outperforming previous estimates. Additionally, the variational approach enables the calculation of the entanglement rank in multipartite states, which subsequently allows for the development of refined criteria to assess entanglement separability. The reliability of this method is demonstrated through detailed analyses of an analectical state and the three-qubit Wiseman state.

A well-documented phenomenon called a small-scale electron temperature gradient driven instability occurs when electrons try to adapt their non-Maxwellian temperature distribution to the system's gradient.  Research has shown that in collisionless slab plasmas, electron temperature differences are driving the growth of electron modes, paired with magnetic reconnection events of a finite-k type, particularly affecting the perpendicular direction.  These tearing modes exhibit characteristics unique to collisionless plasmas, particularly at the electron scale.  Using electron kinetic theory with a hot electron background, we studied the linear growth rates, frequencies, and energy properties of these electron-driven modes across various plasma regimes defined by the electron to ion mass ratio.  We found that these modes have magnetic energy properties that are two orders of magnitude lower than ion modes, making them unlikely drivers of small-scale magnetic reconnection events in plasmas.

A notable achievement in fashion image retrieval is fashion manipulation, which links a query image to a target garment within a vast database. Although fashion manipulation relies on deep learning, a primary challenge lies in its data requirements. Current methods, such as style transfer and disentanglement, aim to generate multiple images with varied styles from a single object image. However, these approaches necessitate either style images or 3D shape information, which are rarely available. As an alternative, we introduce a novel semi-supervised framework for large-scale fashion manipulation, focusing on manipulating style within unknown query images. This innovative framework involves two main components: a shape disentanglement module that utilizes a generator to remove shapes from pairs of images, and a feature-matching module that aligns shape-free features of a query pair. Additionally, we incorporate an image generator to prevent features from becoming style-dependent. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to successfully apply fashion manipulation in a semi-supervised setting, requiring access solely to a fashion dataset. Furthermore, we introduce a novel evaluation metric, ShapeNet-20, a curated dataset of 200,000 articles with known shapes. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, with notable performance metrics including 20.6% mAP, 25.3% MeanRecall, and 75.2% mAP@20 on the NTREND dataset.

The $\R$-optimal solution for the underdetermined equation $Ax=y$ where $A$ is a bounded linear operator mapping a Banach space to another, along with given parameters $\R$ and $y$, is introduced. By utilising dual space properties, optimal solution approximations via dual gradient methods are formulated and analysed for both smooth and non-smooth cases. Furthermore, convergence rate estimates are derived under specific conditions and it is demonstrated that step-size selection influences the convergence order. An example application of this approach also yields a novel algorithm for solving source type inverse problems with inexact data that achieves a predetermined accuracy within a specified time frame.

Constructing the cost function is a crucial step in estimating light field depth but
the problem has not received sufficient attention in literature. The majority of
cost functions used in depth estimation are designed for images, and several
attempt to adapt them for light field data. In this paper, a novel approach is
proposed to address the cost function issue. The proposed approach enables the
utilization of data from multiple views to determine intrinsic depth information.
Additionally, a specific region in light field data that provides valuable
information for cost construction is identified. A deep learning-based solution
is designed to process this area, and its effectiveness is demonstrated by
integrating it with an existing deep learning-based light field depth estimation
method. Experimental results reveal that the proposed approach significantly
improves estimation accuracy, with state-of-the-art performance achieved on LF
datasets.

This study takes advantage of the bilinear technique to investigate the Fokas-Lenells equations, which are written in a specific form involving two complex functions and their spatial-temporal derivatives and combinations. By reducing the equations to the determinant form, we are able to derive two distinct types of Fokus-Lenells solutions, both of which are composed of double poles, and then use this solution framework to construct periodic solutions with multiple peaks. In addition, we use the solutions to create nonlinear superpositions and generate new equations, such as the nonlinear 2D complex modified KdV equation, the nonlinear 2D complex modified KdV equation with a source, the nonlinear 2D complex cosh-Gordon equation, the nonlinear 2D complex sine-Gordon equation, and the nonlinear 2D complex modified Klein-Gordon equation.

Alternative theories of gravity that go beyond the Riemannian framework have been proposed to explore quantum gravity and model systems with non-relativistic symmetry. However, for the most general theories, deriving the action equations can be challenging, especially when parameter space is high-dimensional. This research draws on insights from double field theory and D-brine gravity to establish a method for constructing highly non-linear and non-Riemannian gravity actions. By applying this approach, specific examples of gravity theories are provided, and an analysis is performed to determine the conditions under which the metrics are necessary for a theory to be equivalent to their double field theory counterparts.

In dense home WiFi networks, determining which access point or extender to connect to is a pressing issue. The current approach of relying on signal strength, used by most devices, is insufficient. Many users in dense networks have multiple strong WiFi connections and must manually choose one. Many home WiFi devices, like smart plugs, don't support this feature. Our study proposes a channel-aware method using IEEE 802.11k/v to automatically select the load-lightest access point or extender based on its capabilities. Our solution works on both client devices and networks without needing changes. Experimental results show that using the new algorithm to support around 15 devices in a dense home WiFi results in an average 20% or more improvement in throughput.
